newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - July 24.
newsitem.headline: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - July 24.

text.p: Some Australian stocks to watch this morning:

National Australia Bank (NAB), is forecast to report on Thursday a weaker or, at best, flat quarterly earnings result. Banking analysts told Reuters on Wednesday they expected NAB to report net profit of between A$530 million and A$560 million for the third quarter ended June 30.

Time Warner Inc will put News Corp's Fox News channel on Time's cable TV system, the two companies said on Wednesday, saying they had agreed to settle the dispute between them. As part of the settlement all outstanding litigation between Time and News Corp will be discontinued as well as all litigation between Time Warner and New York City, they said.

Gold miner Acacia Resources Ltd said on Thursday it expected its net profit after abnormals for the half year to June 30 to rise to about A$19 million, compared with A$7.5 million a year ago. Acacia said its half year net profit before abnormals was expected to be about A$13 million, with an abnormal profit after tax of about A$6 million.

Energy Equity Corp Ltd (EEC) said on Thursday the Singa-1 exploration well in South Sumatra, Indonesia, flowed gas at the rate of 30.7 million standard cubic feet per day during a production test. "Based on these results and with more appropriately sized completion tubing installed in the well, EEC expects Singa-1 will produce in excess of 65 million (cubic feet per day) at the likely required delivery pressure," EEC managing director Maurice Brand said in a statement.

Orogen Minerals Ltd said on Wednesday it expected the Moran oil field in PNG to be producing 10,000 barrels per day (bpd) of oil by October this year or shortly after under an extended well test arrangement. Orogen also said on Wednesday it had begun due diligence on acquiring a 10 percent stake in the Ok Tedi copper mine held by the PNG government.

Australian cinema group Hoyts Cinemas Ltd on Wednesday increased the tempo of its expansion into Latin America with a move into the region's biggest market Brazil and neighbouring Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay. Hoyts will fund the entry into the Latin markets through a A$95 million one-for-six rights issue also announced.
Investment bank Macquarie Bank Ltd moved on Wednesday to dampen growing speculation that it was planning a big share buy-back, saying any buy-back would be too small to bolster the share price.
